what.title: What is Supabase?
what.oneliner: Supabase is an open-source Backend-as-a-Service built on PostgreSQL.
what.feature1Desc: Real SQL. Not NoSQL. The world's most advanced open-source database.
what.feature2Desc: Built-in user management with JWT, OAuth, and magic links.
what.feature3Desc: S3-compatible object storage with policies and CDN.
what.feature4Desc: Live updates via WebSockets. Subscribe to any table change.

baas.title: What is BaaS?
baas.description: BaaS lets frontend developers skip server management. Instead of building auth, APIs, and databases from scratch, you connect to a fully managed backend.
baas.benefit: You focus on the product. BaaS handles the plumbing.
baas.traditionalNote: Every layer requires separate setup, auth wiring, and scaling.

examples.title: BaaS Examples
examples.subtitle: You are not alone in choosing managed backends
examples.note: Each has trade-offs. Supabase bets on open standards and PostgreSQL.
examples.firebaseDesc: Google's BaaS. NoSQL, real-time, serverless. Mature ecosystem.
examples.appwriteDesc: Open-source BaaS. Self-hostable. SQL + NoSQL support.
examples.xanoDesc: No-code backend builder. Visual API designer. Postgres underneath.

offers.title: What Supabase Offers
offers.subtitle: A complete backend platform in one place
offers.dbDesc: Full relational DB with extensions: pg_cron, PostGIS, pgvector, and hundreds more.
offers.vectorDesc: pgvector integration for AI embeddings and semantic search out of the box.
offers.authDesc: Email, OAuth, magic links, SSO — with Row Level Security natively integrated.
offers.storageDesc: S3-compatible object storage with CDN, fine-grained policies, and image transforms.
offers.realtimeDesc: Subscribe to DB changes, broadcast messages, and track presence channels.
offers.edgeDesc: Deploy TypeScript / JavaScript functions globally with a Deno runtime.
offers.logsDesc: Query your logs with SQL. Built-in dashboards. No extra observability tooling needed.
offers.selfhostDesc: Full Docker Compose stack available. Own your data. Zero vendor lock-in.
offers.mcpDesc: Connect Supabase workflows with MCP-compatible tools and AI agents.

dx.title: Developer Experience
dx.subtitle: Designed so you can ship, not configure
dx.instantDesc: PostgREST auto-generates a full REST API from your schema. Zero configuration.
dx.sqlDesc: Write real SQL. Version-control your schema with Supabase CLI migrations.
dx.rlsDesc: Row Level Security policies defined in SQL. Your security lives in the database.
dx.dashboardDesc: Manage tables, view logs, and monitor usage — all in the browser.
dx.localDesc: Full local Supabase stack via CLI. Exactly mirrors your production environment.
dx.communityDesc: Best-in-class docs. Active Discord, GitHub discussions, and YouTube channel.

vectormind.title: How Supabase Changed Everything For Portal.mr
vectormind.subtitle: Our job and opportunities platform transformed after moving to Supabase.
vectormind.story1: Portal.mr is a central platform to discover public procurement, tenders, government projects, regulations, and job opportunities.
vectormind.story2: It is open to everyone: businesses, public institutions, suppliers, and professionals.
vectormind.story3: After moving our backend workflows to Supabase, we shipped faster and simplified operations.
vectormind.highlight: Supabase gave Portal.mr a faster and cleaner path from idea to production.
vectormind.reason1: Eliminated boilerplate auth (JWT, sessions, refresh tokens)
vectormind.reason2: pgvector replaced a custom vector store microservice
vectormind.reason3: RLS replaced 400+ lines of hand-coded permission guards
vectormind.reason4: Edge Functions replaced multiple Spring Boot services
vectormind.story4: We also added an AI assistant to guide users and improve discovery across the platform.
vectormind.summary: Portal.mr now runs with Supabase and an AI assistant.

limits.title: Limits & Lessons
limits.subtitle: Real issues from usage and feedback.
limits.limit1Desc: Auth logout with no clear reason in some sessions.
limits.limit2Desc: Client can't fetch more than 1000 rows in one request.
limits.limit3Desc: Realtime updates are sometimes not stable or delayed.
limits.lessonDesc: No tool is perfect. Every technology has limits and occasional issues. But before blaming the tool:
limits.constructive: When something goes wrong, first review the architecture, configuration, and usage before blaming the tool. Often the problem comes from how the system is designed or used. If everything is set up correctly and the issue persists, then it may be a real limitation. In that case, adapt the architecture or complement the tool where needed.
limits.issueNote: Client1000 fetch limit is one I had. Others were mentioned by people. Probably much more.
limits.moreIssuesSubtitle: Storage upload problems, database too slow, vector search results are not good, etc... and probably much more.
